ledger.note: 26 January 1802: the Cisalpine Republic becomes the Italian Republic at the Lyon meetings. Infobox 'National Meetings in Lyon: 26 January 1802'; 'Napoleon Bonaparte served as president and its capital was Milan'; the Legislative Body was 'First appointed at the Meetings of Lyon'. The page gives no separate proclamation date.

17 March 1805: the Republic becomes the Kingdom of Italy. Infobox 'Monarchy proclaimed: 17 March 1805'; 'following Bonaparte's assumption of the title of Emperor of the French, the Italian Republic was transformed into the Kingdom of Italy', with Napoleon as king and Eugène de Beauharnais as viceroy; the Kingdom page: Napoleon was crowned in Milan Cathedral on 23 May. Same state, same colour (rule 2).

'The final territorial change came into effect on 10 June 1810', gaining 'all of southern Tyrol up to Bolzano' (the department of Haut Adige); Bavaria gave it under the Treaty of Schönbrunn of 14 October 1809. [Reviewer eu-20-c, 2026-10-31: confidence lowered from 3 to 2: the page gives 'all the southern Tirol up to the city of Bolzano' and says the department 'mainly corresponds to the province of Trentino including the city of Bolzano', so the whole Bozen province (Vinschgau, Meran, Brixen, Puster valley) is broader than the page names.]

region.text: Istria and the never fully incorporated Dalmatia (and Ragusa), placed in the Illyrian Provinces

ledger.note: 10 June 1810: Istria and Dalmatia go to France. 'Italy lost Istria and the never fully incorporated Dalmatia' (announced by Napoleon on 28 May); by the Treaty of Schönbrunn of 14 October 1809 'Italy ceded Istria, Dalmatia and Ragusa to France', which placed them in the Illyrian Provinces (Illyrian page). That page does not date the transfer and says the lands had been given to Italy 'in 1805 and 1808'.

April-May 1814: Austria takes the Kingdom. 'Eugène surrendered on 23 April, and was exiled to Bavaria by the Austrians, who occupied Milan on 28 April'; 'the remains of the kingdom were annexed by the Austrian Empire as the Kingdom of Lombardy-Venetia', the Treaty of Paris being signed 30 May 1814. The share that went to other states is not given by any page opened.

11 April 1814: Napoleon abdicates the throne of Italy. 'When Napoleon abdicated both the thrones of France and Italy on 11 April 1814', Eugène on the Mincio tried to have himself crowned; he surrendered on 23 April and the Austrians occupied Milan on 28 April.

wars.outcome: Austria's invasion of Italy under Archduke John was beaten at the Piave on 8 May 1809 and he was forced out of Italy; Schönbrunn (14 October 1809) then exchanged Istria, Dalmatia and Ragusa for South Tyrol.
wars.note: The page names Sacile (April), Caldiero (30 April), the Piave (8 May) and Raab, and says nothing on which Italian lands Austria held or for how long.

wars.outcome: Napoleon's abdication (11 April 1814), Eugène's surrender (23 April) and the Austrian occupation of Milan (28 April) ended the Kingdom, annexed by Austria as the Kingdom of Lombardy-Venetia.

certainty.note: The pages name departments and treaties, not boundary lines; the Venetian, Istrian and Dalmatian lines and the 1808 and 1810 additions are approximate regions, and Dalmatia was 'never fully incorporated'.

notes: ROW AND IDENTITY. Cliopatria's 'Italian Republic' row (1803-1813) is Napoleonic Italy: the Italian Republic (26 January 1802 to 17 March 1805) and the Kingdom of Italy (17 March 1805 to April 1814), one continuous state whose change of name is a rename event here. It is not the Republic of Italy of 1946 (row republic-of-italy): both carry Wikidata Q38 and the Wikipedia field 'Italy' in Cliopatria, which is the modern country; wikidata is therefore left null here and the Wikipedia title is the Napoleonic Kingdom's. The eu-13 agent splitting the Kingdom of Italy row (587-1946) should not write another Napoleonic Kingdom of Italy; this dossier is its home. CLIOPATRIA ERRORS. The 1803 and 1805 shapes are fine, but the 1806-1810 shapes (about 47,000 km2) leave out Venetia (annexed 1806), Istria and Dalmatia (1806-June 1810), the Marches (April 1808) and South Tyrol (June 1810); only the 1811-1813 shape (84,881 km2) holds the maximum extent. Four new keyframes (1802, 1808, 1810, 1814) fill the years Cliopatria lacks. The 1806 and 1809 corrections use the region Dalmatia (12,139 km2), a generous placement of a land the page says was 'never fully incorporated'; Ragusa is left out of the corrections: the Illyrian page says it was 'adjudicated to the Napoleonic Kingdom of Italy in 1805 and 1808' and the Kingdom page lists it only among the lands Italy ceded in 1809-1810, never among its gains, so its status in 1806-1810 is open. The infobox area (53,000 km2 for 1808) conflicts with the page's own 84,000 km2 peak and with the corrected 1808 land (about 89,000 km2); the doubtful figure is the infobox. COUNTERPARTS. habsburg-monarchy is the loser of Venetia (its row ends 1805; austrian-empire begins 1806); papal-states of the Marches; kingdom-of-bavaria of South Tyrol; first-french-empire (Illyrian Provinces) takes Istria and Dalmatia. The Cispadane Republic row (1800-1802) and the Cisalpine Republic row (1797-1799) are other agents' work; the Subalpine Republic (infobox predecessor) has no row. After 1814 the Marches, Emilia and other lands left the Austrian share: no page opened covers it. Page budget: six pages opened for 10 shapes.
